classification.habitat: Temperate habitats; recorded from the Mediterranean to Iran in current Kew POWO
classification.distribution: Native from the Mediterranean to Iran; introduced in multiple temperate regions

identification.description: Erect annual or biennial herb, up to about 80 cm, densely covered with viscid glandular hairs; lower leaves are petiolate and upper leaves become sessile and clasp the stem.
identification_points: Viscid glandular hairs covering the plant.
Lower leaves petiolate; upper leaves sessile/amplexicaul.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Hyoscyamus niger L. is an accepted Solanaceae species in Kew POWO; the genus Hyoscyamus is documented as a source of tropane alkaloids including hyoscyamine and scopolamine. This record is for botanical and educational reference and does not provide clinical dosing.
modern_information.safety_notes: Poisonous/tropane-alkaloid-containing plant group; do not infer clinical treatment or dosing from this educational record. Verify authoritative toxicology and pharmacopoeial guidance.

exam_points: Botanical identity: Hyoscyamus niger L.; Family: Solanaceae; annual or biennial habit and glandular-hairy, sticky foliage are useful diagnostic features.
